bench_setup = function() {
	set.seed(20261117)
	n = 200L
	w = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5); x1 = rnorm(n)
	X = cbind(treatment = w, x1 = x1)
	t_ev = stats::rexp(n, rate = exp(0.3 * w - 0.2 * x1))
	t_c = stats::rexp(n, rate = 0.3)
	y = round(pmin(t_ev, t_c), 2)
	y[y <= 0] = 0.01
	dead = as.numeric(t_ev <= t_c)
	strata = c(rep(seq_len(70L), each = 2L), rep(71L, n - 140L))
	list(X = X, y = y, dead = dead, strata = strata, b_null = c(0.3, -0.2), delta = 0.3)
}

breslow_hazard_cumsum = function(y, dead, X, b_null){
	if (length(y) == 0L || sum(dead) == 0L) return(list(times = numeric(0), cumhaz = numeric(0)))
	eta = as.numeric(X %*% b_null)
	risk = exp(eta - max(eta))
	o = order(y, -dead)
	y_o = y[o]; dead_o = dead[o] > 0.5; risk_o = risk[o]
	event_times = unique(y_o[dead_o])
	if (length(event_times) == 0L) return(list(times = numeric(0), cumhaz = numeric(0)))
	rc = rev(cumsum(rev(risk_o)))
	R_k = rc[match(event_times, y_o)]
	d_k = tabulate(match(y_o[dead_o], event_times), nbins = length(event_times))
	list(times = event_times, cumhaz = cumsum(d_k / pmax(R_k, 1e-10)))
}
cox_nll_breslow_cumsum = function(X, y, dead, beta, strata = NULL){
	X = as.matrix(X); y = as.numeric(y); dead = as.numeric(dead); beta = as.numeric(beta)
	if (length(beta) != ncol(X)) return(NA_real_)
	s = if (is.null(strata)) rep.int(1L, length(y)) else as.integer(strata)
	eta = as.numeric(X %*% beta)
	if (!all(is.finite(eta))) return(NA_real_)
	n = length(y)
	o = order(s, y)
	s_o = s[o]; y_o = y[o]; e_o = eta[o]; ev_o = dead[o] == 1
	m = max(e_o)
	rc = stats::ave(exp(e_o - m), s_o, FUN = function(v) rev(cumsum(rev(v))))
	new_grp = c(TRUE, s_o[-1L] != s_o[-n] | y_o[-1L] != y_o[-n])
	start = which(new_grp)[cumsum(new_grp)]
	log_den = log(rc[start]) + m
	-sum(e_o[ev_o] - log_den[ev_o])
}
bench_run = function(d) {
	bh = breslow_hazard_cumsum(d$y, d$dead, d$X, d$b_null)
	nll = cox_nll_breslow_cumsum(d$X[, 1L, drop = FALSE], d$y, d$dead, d$delta, strata = d$strata)
	list(times = as.numeric(bh$times), cumhaz = as.numeric(bh$cumhaz), nll = as.numeric(nll))
}

Results differ only in summation order (and the candidate NLL's max-shift inside log-sum), so the closed_form 1e-10 tier applies.
